source: ARCHIVE_DB cc49101c-0569-4d41-8e7a-be139cde4f26, table briefs, read-only SELECT through the Cloudflare D1 tool, counts only (no brief text copied)
sql: SELECT sport, COUNT(*) briefs, SUM(brief_text LIKE '%-point margin%' OR '%-points margin%') points_margin, SUM(brief_text LIKE '%-goal margin%' OR '%-goals margin%') goal_margin, SUM(brief_text LIKE '%series record%' OR '%series matchup%' OR '%aggregate series%') series_wording, MIN(date), MAX(date) FROM briefs WHERE brief_type='night_owl' AND date >= '2026-10-27' AND sport IN (<the soccer labels>) GROUP BY sport
note: SQLite LIKE is the stand-in for the CC-CMD's regexes: a brief that says '4-points margin' or '1-point margin' counts as points_margin. The queried labels with no night_owl row in the window (UEFA Europa Conference League, EFL Cup, EFL Trophy, FA Cup) are absent from the result.
reading: MLS is the one soccer label whose _sport ('MLS Soccer') contains a word the two margin-unit chains test for ('soccer', 'mls'). It has 0 points_margin briefs of 34. Every other soccer label has them: 252 of 410 briefs. That is the cause the CC-CMD hypothesised, measured as a natural experiment. The 'goal margin' briefs in the other labels are the model following the prompt's other line, 'Sport: Football (soccer). Score in GOALS (NEVER "points")', over the MARGIN line that says points: the same prompt carries both.
